challenges.name: personal-data-quiz
challenges.title: Can another learner see this?
challenges.description: A course page split into a cached part and a per-request part, and an API response with a public Cache-Control: decide what two different learners receive.

questions.explanation: True. getPublicCourse takes only the course id and reads nothing about the user, so its cached result is the same for everyone and safe to share; it is cached per id with the course tag. LearnerPanel reads the session cookie, which makes it dynamic: it runs for every request and its output is never stored in the shared cache, and it computes the coupon price from the public list price inside one request. The misconception is that a page is either cached for everyone or for nobody; splitting by component lets the expensive public part be shared while the personal part stays per request.

questions.question:
$ curl -si https://api.codedev.test/course-page/42 -H "Cookie: session=LAN_SESSION"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=300
Vary: Accept-Encoding
Content-Type: application/json

{"course":{"id":"42","title":"Next.js Rendering & Caching"},"enrollment":{"progress":35},"price":249000}

A CDN that honours Cache-Control sits in front of the API.

Statement: "Because the request carries Lan's session cookie, the CDN keeps a separate copy for each learner, so Binh cannot receive Lan's progress from it."
questions.explanation: False. A shared cache keys a stored response by the URL and by the request headers named in Vary. Vary names only Accept-Encoding, and public, s-maxage=300 explicitly allows shared caches to store the response, so Binh's request for the same URL within 300 seconds can be answered with Lan's copy, progress included. The fix is to split the data: a public endpoint for the course with public caching, and a personal endpoint with Cache-Control: private, no-store. The misconception is that cookies automatically partition caches; they only do if the cache is configured to key on them, which also destroys the hit rate.

challenges.name: split-public-and-personal-data
challenges.title: Compose the course page from shared and personal data
challenges.description: The course page response used to mix course data with the learner's progress and coupon price and was cached for everyone; learners saw each other's progress. Write renderCoursePage(req, ttl, deps), which returns the page text for one request { at (seconds), userId (null for an anonymous visitor), courseId }. Public data: deps.sharedCache is one cache shared by every request of every user (values are stored as JSON). Keep the public course { id, title, price, lessons } there under the key course:<courseId> together with the time you stored it; it is fresh while at < storedAt + ttl. When it is missing or no longer fresh, call deps.loadPublicCourse(courseId) once and store the result. If the loader returns null, return "404 Not Found", store nothing and load nothing else. Personal data is never written to the shared cache and is loaded on every request that needs it: for a signed-in learner call deps.loadEnrollment(userId, courseId) first; only if they are not enrolled call deps.loadCoupon(userId). Anonymous visitors cause no personal loads. A coupon { code, percent, courses, expiresAt } applies when percent is an integer from 1 to 100, at < expiresAt, and courses is "all" or contains the course id; the price after it is Math.round(price * (100 - percent) / 100). Page text, with H = "<title> | <lessons> lessons": anonymous, or signed in without an applicable coupon -> "H | <price> VND | Enroll"; enrolled -> "H | Enrolled, <progress>% complete"; with an applicable coupon -> "H | <new price> VND with coupon <code> (list <price> VND) | Enroll". Requests arrive in time order. The runner prints each page with the loads it caused (public:<id>, enrollment:<user>:<id>, coupon:<user>), then the keys of the shared cache and the number of public loads.
hints: For each value on the page, ask: would it be the same if another person sent this request? Only the values where the answer is yes may go through deps.sharedCache; everything else is loaded for this request and forgotten.

Look at what you store under course:<id>: the course and the time you stored it, nothing derived from the user. Then look at the order of the personal loads: anonymous visitors stop before any of them, and an enrolled learner stops before the coupon. The freshness check uses < at the boundary, so an entry stored at 0 with ttl 300 is reloaded at 300.

A similar split on the lesson page, with ttl 60: the lesson body is public and cached as lesson:<id>; a learner's notes are personal. Requests at 0 (Lan), 30 (anonymous) and 60 (Binh) for lesson 9 give the loads [public:9 notes:lan:9], [] and [public:9 notes:binh:9], and the shared cache ends with the single key lesson:9: Binh never sees Lan's notes and the body was loaded once per minute.
